name: Stropharia rugosoannulata

tip_speed.note: Hao H et al. 2022 (AMB Express 12:56, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13568-022-01400-2) give 0.293 and 0.181 for strains DQ-1 and DQ-3 on PDA at 25 C, printed as mm/d. Taken as printed that is 12 and 8 um/h, which would need months to cover a plate, so the unit is read here as cm/d: mean 2.37 mm/day x 41.7 = 99 um/h. Supported by per-strain regressions of growth rate on temperature in Chen X-T et al. 2021 (Mycosystema 40:3081-3095, Table 4, units not shown on the page opened), which give about 2.3 to 2.7 at 25 C. Needs checking against a source with clear units

t_opt.note: review, citing Chinese cultivation literature (Yan et al. 2001; Chen et al. 2021): mycelium grows from 5 to 35 C with the optimum at 26 C
t_opt.source: Huang L, Si C, He C-M, Liu X-C, Duan J 2025, The rise of Stropharia rugosoannulata industry in China: current state and prospects, Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology 109:188

t_min.note: review: growth stops below 5 C though the mycelium survives
t_min.source: Huang L, Si C, He C-M, Liu X-C, Duan J 2025, The rise of Stropharia rugosoannulata industry in China: current state and prospects, Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology 109:188

t_max.note: review: above 35 C the mycelium is inhibited or killed. Strains differ: 5 to 34 C for a heat-sensitive strain and 5 to 42 C for a heat-tolerant one (Ren J et al. 2021, Mycoscience 62:95-105, https://doi.org/10.47371/mycosci.2020.11.006)
t_max.source: Huang L, Si C, He C-M, Liu X-C, Duan J 2025, The rise of Stropharia rugosoannulata industry in China: current state and prospects, Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology 109:188

cold_drop.note: primordia form at 10 to 20 C and the mycelial optimum is 26 C (Huang et al. 2025, Appl Microbiol Biotechnol 109:188, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00253-025-13576-1, citing Stamets and Chilton 1983); 26 - 20 = 6 C is the smallest drop that reaches that range

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

size_cm.note: cap width. Caps up to 25 cm are reported in cultivation (Huang et al. 2025, Appl Microbiol Biotechnol 109:188)

notes: Thick white cords in mulch; cultivated outdoors. Reported (unchecked) to have spiny cells that kill nematodes; its relative S. caerulea is a Boddy-lab cord species [15].
